segments.text: If you have tried to meditate and it never really stuck, this is a different thing.
Autogenic training is physical. You repeat one short phrase to yourself. My right arm is heavy.
And after a few days, the arm actually does feel heavy. You notice it happen.
There is nothing to concentrate on. Trying is the one thing that reliably blocks it.
What you are training is deliberate access to a state your body normally only reaches on its own.
Not to relax right now. To be able to.
People notice it in ordinary places. Less noise in the head — not silence, the volume down.
Coming down faster after a bad day, instead of staying wound up for hours.
Getting to sleep. And a clearer head between two demanding things.
There are six exercises, and you learn them in order.
Heaviness in the arms and legs. Then warmth. Then the heartbeat, the breath, the warmth of your centre, and a cool forehead.
About a week on each, one short phrase at a time.
The practice itself is ninety seconds, three times a day. Short and often — frequency is what builds it, not length.
Each phrase is guided for your first few days. Then it is only a timer. Then nothing at all.
Because the point is that you end up not needing this.
You move on when your own record says it is landing, and you can run it with nothing playing. A week is the least it takes, not the whole of it.
And expect nothing for the first few days. That is normal. Trying harder is the one thing that reliably blocks it.
That is everything. Start with the first phrase.
